H_hierarchical.evidence: The paper names automatic and manual operating modes, plus initialization/main/fault program modules, but does not define explicit nested parent-child states.

G_guards_arith.evidence: The control flow branches on selected layer, lower-space vacancy, vehicle presence/position sensors, and the disjunctive fault condition: too long OR overweight OR other security risks.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: Actions include lift/traverse motor commands, automatic reset, sound-light alarm, stopping all actions, clearing all ports, and prompting troubleshooting.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: The fault alarm program triggers on overlength/overweight/security risk and globally stops all actions, clears ports, alarms, and prompts troubleshooting.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: Automatic/manual modes are introduced in section 2.1, sensor and actuator qualifications in section 3.2, and detailed access/fault behavior in section 3.3.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Terms such as manual/point operation, anti-falling electromagnet, safety hook, and fault alarm require decoding garage/PLC safety semantics.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: Mode names are not paired with a state table; actions such as move carriers, drop tray, reset, alarm, stop, and clear ports are described narratively across later prose.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: The fault branch combines multiple conditions: vehicle too long, overweight, or other security risks; access also depends on selected layer and lower-space vacancy.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: No explicit composite state with parent-level entry/during/exit behavior is described.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: On fault, the system stops all actions and clears all ports, implying a cross-cutting escape from ongoing lift/traverse operations.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: No deep composite state or non-trivial composite initialization chain is specified.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: There are guard combinations over layer choice, lower-space vacancy, sensor states, and a disjunctive fault condition, but no rich arithmetic guard set.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: The fault alarm rule applies globally to ongoing operations and can be encoded once as a forced cross-cutting transition instead of duplicating transitions from lift, traverse, direct-access, and reset states.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: Most actions are concrete motor/alarm/port outputs, but operation monitoring and troubleshooting prompt are abstract operator-facing side effects.

key_nl_quotes: The main operating modes of the control system are divided into two types, automatic operation mode and manual operation mode.

When the vehicle is too long or overweight, or there are some other security risks, the fault alarm program will be sent to the sound and light signal alarm, while the system will stop all actions, clear all ports and prompt troubleshooting.
one_line_pitch: A compact PLC garage controller stresses baselines through sensor-guarded lift/shift sequencing plus a global fault-alarm escape that must stop and clear every ongoing action.
rationale: This is a meaningful stress-test because the paper gives enough operational detail to build an EFSM with mode selection, layer-dependent guarded routing, motor/output actions, reset behavior, and a global fault branch. Its main weakness is limited explicit hierarchy, but the guard/action/fault dimensions directly target known low-F1 baseline components. The cross-section prose layout and global stop-clear-alarm rule make it especially prone to semantic omissions in Umple-style single-prompt or syntax-repair baselines.
